examples.ko: 우리 팀은 곧바로 공격할 태세를 갖췄어요.
examples.en: Our team got ready to attack right away.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 비상 대비 태세에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: Because of the heavy rain, we went into emergency readiness.

examples.ko: 그는 금방이라도 화낼 태세로 서 있었어요.
examples.en: He stood there looking ready to get angry at any moment.
The fire station keeps a 24-hour readiness to respond.

examples.ko: 출동 태세가 항상 갖춰져 있어서 안심이 돼요.
examples.en: It's reassuring that they are always ready to be dispatched.
The cat looks ready to jump at any moment.

explain: '준비'와 달리 '태세'는 바로 행동에 들어갈 수 있는 몸과 마음의 자세를 말해요. '~할 태세다'로 곧 하려는 모습을 말하고, '비상 태세', '방어 태세', '임전 태세'처럼 굳은 말로도 자주 써요. '갖추다', '유지하다', '취하다' 같은 말과 함께 나와요.

phrases.en: The players switched to a defensive stance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공격을 막으려고 준비한 자세를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a stance prepared to block an attack.

phrases.en: The soldiers waited in readiness for battle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 싸울 준비를 마친 모습을 뜻하는 굳은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression for being fully ready to fight.

phrases.en: The child looks ready to cry any moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 어떤 행동을 할 것 같은 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone looks about to do something.

explain_en: Unlike '준비' (preparation), '태세' is the stance, physical or mental, of being ready to act right away. '~할 태세다' describes someone about to do something, and it also appears in set phrases like '비상 태세' and '방어 태세'. It pairs with verbs such as '갖추다', '유지하다' and '취하다'.

examples.ko: 다들 좋은 자리를 차지하려고 혈안이 돼 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone is desperately trying to take a good spot.

examples.ko: 그는 돈을 버는 데 혈안이 되어 가족도 잊었어요.
examples.en: He was so obsessed with making money that he forgot his family.

examples.ko: 사람들이 할인 상품을 사려고 혈안이 돼서 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: People lined up frantically to buy the discounted goods.

examples.ko: 남의 잘못을 찾는 데만 혈안이 된 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: There are people who are only fixated on finding others' faults.
Reporters were frantic to get a scoop.

examples.ko: 왜 그렇게 이기는 데 혈안이 되었어요?
examples.en: Why are you so obsessed with winning?

explain: '혈안이 되다'라는 꼴로 거의 항상 쓰고, 눈이 충혈될 만큼 한 가지에만 매달린다는 뜻이에요. 대부분 좋지 않게 보는 시선이 담겨 있어서 칭찬할 때는 쓰지 않아요. 그냥 '열심히 하다'와 달리 지나치다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: to be desperately set on something, to be frantic about getting it
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이 충혈될 정도로 한 가지 목적에만 매달리는 모습이에요. 보통 욕심이 지나치다는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes clinging to one goal until your eyes go bloodshot. It usually carries a negative feel of excessive greed.

explain_en: It is almost always used as '혈안이 되다', meaning to cling to one thing so hard that your eyes turn bloodshot. It usually carries a disapproving view, so you don't use it to praise someone. Unlike plain '열심히 하다' (to work hard), it feels excessive.

examples.ko: 오래 앉아 있으면 견갑골 주변이 뻐근해요.
examples.en: If I sit for a long time, the area around my shoulder blades gets stiff.
The doctor said there is a crack in my shoulder blade.

examples.ko: 이 운동은 견갑골을 모아 주는 자세가 중요해요.
examples.en: In this exercise, the posture of squeezing the shoulder blades together is important.
My shoulder blades look sticking out, and it bothers me.
Try pointing to where your shoulder blade is with your hand.
I carried a heavy bag, and even my shoulder blades hurt.

explain: 병원이나 운동 이야기에서 많이 쓰는 말이고, 쉬운 우리말로는 '날개뼈'라고 해요. 등 위쪽, 어깨 뒤에 있는 뼈를 가리켜요. '견갑골 운동'처럼 헬스 이야기에도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: My shoulder blade hurt, so I got a massage.
phrases.nuance_ko: '견갑골'의 쉬운 우리말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The plain Korean word for 견갑골.

phrases.en: My shoulder blade hurts when I drive for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 아픈 곳을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used at the hospital to say where it hurts.

phrases.en: I stretch my shoulder blades before studying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동이나 건강 이야기에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in exercise and health talk.

explain_en: It is common in talk about hospitals and exercise, and the plainer Korean word is '날개뼈'. It points to the bone at the upper back behind the shoulder. It also often appears in fitness talk, as in '견갑골 운동'.

examples.ko: 선수들이 대회를 앞두고 구슬땀을 흘리며 훈련해요.
examples.en: The players train, dripping with sweat, ahead of the tournament.

examples.ko: 더운 날 이마에 구슬땀이 송골송골 맺혔어요.
examples.en: On the hot day, beads of sweat formed on my forehead.
I worked without even a moment to wipe away the sweat.
The sweat the farmers shed was not in vain.
My shirt got completely soaked with sweat.

examples.ko: 구슬땀 흘린 만큼 좋은 결과가 나올 거예요.
examples.en: You'll get good results in proportion to the sweat you put in.

explain: 구슬처럼 맺힌 굵은 땀방울인데, 보통 '구슬땀을 흘리다'로 써서 열심히 노력하는 모습을 칭찬해요. 그냥 더워서 나는 땀은 '땀'이라고 해요. 운동, 일, 훈련 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 매일 구슬땀을 흘린 덕에 시험에 합격했어요.
phrases.en: Thanks to working hard every day, I passed the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더워서 땀이 나는 것만이 아니라 힘들게 열심히 노력한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Beyond sweating from heat, it means working or training with great effort.
phrases.en_equiv: sweat it out; put in hard effort

explain_en: It refers to big sweat drops that bead up like marbles, and it is usually used as '구슬땀을 흘리다' to praise someone working hard. Plain sweat from heat is just '땀'. It often appears when talking about sports, work, and training.

t90.ax: My shirt got completely soaked with sweat.

examples.en: The hospital gave the patient a blood transfusion.

examples.ko: 사고로 피를 많이 흘려서 바로 수혈해야 해요.
examples.en: A lot of blood was lost in the accident, so a transfusion must be given right away.
Before giving a transfusion, they check the blood type.
The doctor is getting ready to give a transfusion.
I heard they gave a transfusion during yesterday's surgery.
After a blood transfusion, the body gets much better.

explain: '수혈하다'는 '환자에게 수혈하다'처럼 피를 넣어 주는 쪽에서 써요. 받는 사람 입장에서는 '수혈을 받다'라고 해요. 피를 내주는 일은 '헌혈하다'예요.

phrases.en: The injured person received a blood transfusion at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피를 받는 사람 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person receiving blood.

phrases.en: The doctor gave the patient a blood transfusion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환자에게 피를 넣어 주는 의사나 간호사 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the one who gives the transfusion, such as a doctor or nurse.

phrases.example: 수술 중에 수혈이 필요할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: A blood transfusion may be needed during surgery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피가 모자라서 넣어야 할 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when blood is lacking and must be given.

explain_en: '수혈하다' is used from the side giving blood to the patient, as in '환자에게 수혈하다'. From the patient's side, you say '수혈을 받다'. Donating blood is '헌혈하다'.

examples.en: I wrapped my knee, which I hurt in a fall, with a bandage.

examples.ko: 추워서 목도리로 얼굴을 꽁꽁 싸매고 나갔어요.
examples.en: It was cold, so I went out with my face wrapped up tightly in a scarf.
His finger was cut, so I wrapped it up with a handkerchief for him.

examples.ko: 상처를 싸매기 전에 먼저 깨끗이 씻으세요.
examples.en: Wash the wound clean before you bandage it.
She wrapped the baby in a blanket and carried him.
He came to school with his leg bandaged up.

explain: 다친 곳이나 몸의 일부를 천이나 붕대로 감싸서 묶는다는 느낌이에요. '감다'보다 전체를 덮어 싼다는 느낌이 강해요. '머리를 싸매다'는 관용적으로도 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 시험 문제 때문에 모두 머리를 싸매고 고민했어요.
phrases.en: Everyone racked their brains over the exam question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 머리를 감싸는 게 아니라, 어려운 일을 해결하려고 온 힘을 다해 생각하거나 공부한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It doesn't mean wrapping your head; it means thinking or studying with all your effort to solve something hard.

explain_en: It means covering and tying up an injured spot or body part with cloth or a bandage. It feels more like wrapping the whole thing than '감다' (to wind around). '머리를 싸매다' is also a very common idiom.

examples.ko: 겨울이 오기 전에 독감 백신을 접종해요.
examples.en: I get a flu shot before winter comes.
I got the child the necessary vaccines on time.

examples.ko: 백신을 접종하고 나서 하루 정도 쉬었어요.
examples.en: After getting the vaccine, I rested for about a day.

examples.ko: 접종하기 전에 의사 선생님께 몸 상태를 말해야 해요.
examples.en: Before vaccination, you need to tell the doctor how you feel.
I heard the school is vaccinating students in groups.

examples.ko: 접종한 팔이 조금 아파서 무거운 걸 못 들어요.
examples.en: The arm I got the shot in is a bit sore, so I can't lift heavy things.

explain: 접종하다는 몸에 백신을 넣어서 병을 예방한다는 말이에요. 맞는 사람 쪽에서는 '접종을 받다', '백신을 맞다', '주사 맞다'라고 해요. 의사나 병원 쪽에서는 '접종하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I got vaccinated at the hospital yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맞는 사람 쪽에서 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person receiving the shot.

phrases.en: I'm getting a flu vaccine tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가장 쉽고 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easiest and most natural phrase in everyday talk.

phrases.example: 접종 후에는 열이 날 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You may get a fever after vaccination.
phrases.nuance_ko: '접종'을 명사로 써서 때를 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '접종' to talk about timing.

explain_en: It means putting a vaccine into the body to prevent disease. The person receiving it says '접종을 받다', '백신을 맞다' or '주사 맞다'. The doctor's or hospital's side uses 접종하다.

examples.en: Time heals the wounds of the heart.
This music heals tired people.
That book healed my heart.

examples.ko: 아픈 마음을 치유하는 데는 시간이 필요해요.
examples.en: Healing a hurt heart takes time.

examples.ko: 산책을 하면서 스스로를 치유할 수 있었어요.
examples.en: I was able to heal myself while taking walks.
We created this program to help heal the children.

explain: '치유하다'는 몸의 병뿐 아니라 마음의 상처에도 많이 써요. 병원에서 병을 고칠 때는 '치료하다'가 일반적이에요. '고치다'도 쓰지만 물건이나 습관에 더 어울려요.

phrases.en: Conversation heals emotional wounds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음의 상처와 함께 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used with emotional wounds.

phrases.en: The doctor treats the patient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 병을 고칠 때는 '치료하다'가 일반적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 치료하다 is the usual word for medical treatment.

phrases.en: Right now I need time to heal.
phrases.nuance_ko: '치유'를 명사로 써서 회복하는 시간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 치유 as a noun for a period of recovery.

explain_en: 치유하다 is used for emotional wounds as much as for bodily illness. For a hospital treating a disease, 치료하다 is the usual word. 고치다 also works, but it fits objects and habits better.

dis.h: heal, especially wounds of the heart
gh: give medical care to cure an illness
a doctor sees and treats patients
give quick first-aid care on the spot

p.n: 치료하다 is clinical and does not fit emotional wounds well.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 무거운 짐도 거뜬히 견디는 튼튼한 소재예요.
examples.en: This bag is made of a sturdy material that easily holds heavy loads.

examples.ko: 이 정도 업무량은 신입 사원도 거뜬히 소화할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even a new employee can handle this much work with ease.
My cold cleared up easily in just one day.
That athlete lifts even 100 kilograms without difficulty.

examples.ko: 시험 범위가 많아도 이틀이면 거뜬히 끝낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even if the exam covers a lot, I can finish it easily in two days.

examples.ko: 할머니는 여든이 넘으셨는데도 산을 거뜬히 오르세요.
examples.en: My grandmother is over eighty, but she climbs mountains with ease.

explain: 힘들 것 같은 일을 쉽게 해내거나 몸이 가뿐하게 나을 때 써요. '들다, 이기다, 나아지다' 같은 동사와 함께 쓸 수 있고, 형용사는 '거뜬하다'예요.

phrases.example: 이 정도 짐은 거뜬하게 들 수 있어요.
phrases.en: I can lift this much luggage with ease.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거뜬히'와 같은 뜻이고, 형용사 '거뜬하다'에서 나온 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as the headword, derived from the adjective 거뜬하다.

phrases.en: After a good sleep, my body feels light and fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어와 달리 몸이나 상태가 가뿐하다고 말하는 형용사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adjective describing a body or condition that feels light and refreshed.

phrases.en: I got even a difficult job done without trouble.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 일을 쉽게 마쳤다고 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for finishing a hard task easily.

explain_en: Use it when something that looks hard is done easily, or when the body recovers lightly. It goes with verbs like 들다, 이기다 and 나아지다, and the adjective form is '거뜬하다'.

examples.en: The firefighters brought the fire under control with desperate effort.
He prepared for the exam with a do-or-die resolve.
I ran desperately to save the child.
It was the last game, so the players' faces looked desperate.
My mother's opposition was so fierce that I dropped the plan.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 결사적 수비로 한 골 차 승리를 지켰어요.
examples.en: Our team protected a one-goal win with desperate defense.

explain: '필사적'과 거의 같은 상황에서 쓰고, 반대, 저항, 수비처럼 무언가에 맞서는 말과 잘 어울려요. '결사적 노력'처럼 명사 앞에도 오고 '결사적으로', '결사적인'으로도 써요.

phrases.en: The players defended the goal desperately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 앞에서 목숨을 걸 듯 필사적으로 한다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a verb to add the sense of doing it with all one's might.

phrases.en: The residents put up desperate resistance to the construction.
phrases.nuance_ko: '저항, 반대'처럼 맞서는 말과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs well with words of opposition like resistance.

phrases.example: 팀은 결사적 수비로 1점 차 승리를 지켰어요.
phrases.en: The team protected its one-point win with desperate defense.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 경기에서 끝까지 막아 내는 모습을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in sports for holding on to the very end.

explain_en: It is used in almost the same situations as '필사적' and goes well with words about standing against something, like opposition, resistance and defense. It appears before nouns as in '결사적 노력', and also as '결사적으로' or '결사적인'.

en: to be firm; to be steadfast

examples.ko: 그 아이는 몸은 작아도 마음이 굳세요.
examples.en: That child is small, but strong in spirit.
With a steadfast will, I ran to the end and finished the race.

examples.ko: 어머니는 힘든 일이 있어도 굳세게 버티셨어요.
examples.en: My mother held on steadfastly even through hard times.

examples.ko: 큰 꿈을 이루려면 마음이 굳세어야 해요.
examples.en: To achieve a big dream, your heart has to be strong.
The players stayed steadfast to the end even while losing.
I was ashamed of myself for not being strong.

explain: 주로 사람의 마음, 의지, 태도가 흔들리지 않고 강할 때 써요. 힘이 센 것을 말하는 '세다'와 달리 몸의 힘보다 마음에 초점이 있어요. '굳세게 살아라'처럼 격려하는 말로도 써요.

phrases.en: I prepared for the exam with a steadfast heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: '굳센'으로 바꾸면 명사를 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Changing to 굳센 lets it describe a noun.

phrases.en: Even when it's hard, I hold on strongly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사로 쓰면 '버티다', '살다' 같은 동사와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: As an adverb it goes well with verbs like 버티다 and 살다.

phrases.en: That athlete looks really tough-minded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습에서 마음이 강하다는 느낌을 받을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone's appearance gives a sense of inner strength.

explain_en: It is mostly used for a person's heart, will or attitude that stays strong. Unlike '세다' (strong), the focus is on mental strength, not body strength. It also appears in encouragement like '굳세게 살아라'.

t90.ax: That child is small, but strong in spirit.

examples.ko: 그는 큰 병에도 끄떡없이 일을 계속해요.
examples.en: He keeps working unfazed even after a serious illness.

examples.ko: 이 집은 태풍에도 끄떡없이 서 있어요.
examples.en: This house stands unshaken even in a typhoon.
Even after working all night, she's smiling as if nothing happened.

examples.ko: 아무리 놀려도 그는 끄떡없이 자기 일을 해요.
examples.en: No matter how much they tease him, he calmly does his own work.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 비가 와도 끄떡없이 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can use this bag with no problem even in the rain.
Grandfather is over ninety but still walks with no trouble.

explain: 충격이나 어려움이 있어도 아무 문제 없이 멀쩡한 모습을 말해요. '끄덕이다'(고개를 끄덕이다)와 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 이 말은 '끄떡없다'가 기본형이에요.

phrases.en: This much rain is nothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '끄떡없다'의 해요체로, 아무 문제 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form of '끄떡없다', meaning there's no problem at all.

phrases.en: Grandfather climbs the mountain with unshakable stamina.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 튼튼하고 강한 것을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it describes something sturdy and strong.

phrases.en: This building withstood the earthquake without a problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 충격을 받아도 멀쩡하게 버티는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes holding up unharmed even after a shock.

explain_en: It describes staying completely fine despite a shock or hardship. It is easy to confuse with '끄덕이다' (to nod), but this word comes from '끄떡없다'.

examples.en: I polished my shoes and now they shine glossily.
It only looks slick on the outside, and the inside is not great.
Oil got on my hand and it became greasy and shiny.
He must have put oil on his hair, since it shines glossily.
Be careful of ads that are wrapped up so slickly.
The newly polished floor gleams smoothly.

explain: 기름기나 윤기가 돌아 매끈하게 빛나는 모양이에요. 비유로 겉만 그럴듯하고 속은 비었다는 부정적인 느낌으로도 많이 써요. 보통 '번드르르하다' 모양으로 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 말만 번드르르해서 믿을 수가 없어요.
phrases.en: He is all talk, so I can't trust him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말은 그럴듯하게 잘하지만 실제 행동이나 실속이 없다고 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize someone who speaks smoothly but has no real action or substance behind the words.

explain_en: It describes a smooth shine from oil or gloss. Figuratively, it often has a negative feel of looking good only on the outside while being empty inside. It is usually used in the form '번드르르하다'.

t90.ax: The newly polished floor gleams smoothly.

examples.en: Raising a child takes a lot of patience.
In a marathon, endurance matters as much as physical strength.
After waiting so long, my patience ran out.

examples.ko: 그는 인내력이 강해서 쉽게 포기하지 않아요.
examples.en: He has strong endurance and doesn't give up easily.
To build your perseverance, start with small goals.

examples.ko: 동생은 인내력이 약해서 공부를 금방 그만둬요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has little endurance and quits studying quickly.

explain: '참을성'과 비슷하지만 '인내력'은 조금 더 격식 있고, 참고 견디는 힘이라는 능력 느낌이 있어요. '인내력이 강하다/약하다/필요하다'처럼 써요. 마음가짐을 말할 때는 '인내심'을 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 인내력이 강해서 끝까지 뛰어요.
phrases.en: That athlete has strong endurance and runs to the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참고 견디는 힘이 크다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise someone for a great ability to endure.

phrases.example: 저는 인내력이 부족해서 오래 공부하기 힘들어요.
phrases.en: I lack patience, so studying for a long time is hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금만 힘들어도 쉽게 포기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone gives up easily at slight difficulty.

phrases.en: The teacher teaches the children with patience.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력보다 마음가짐을 말할 때 '인내력' 대신 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used instead of 인내력 when talking about mindset rather than ability.

explain_en: It is similar to '참을성' but a bit more formal, with a feel of an ability or strength to endure. You say '인내력이 강하다/약하다/필요하다'. When talking about mindset, '인내심' is also used.

t90.ax: Raising a child takes a lot of patience.

en: to renew; to reform; to be reformed

examples.ko: 새 사장이 오면서 회사 분위기가 일신했어요.
examples.en: With the new president, the company's atmosphere was completely renewed.

examples.ko: 가게 간판을 바꿔 이미지를 일신하려고 해요.
examples.en: I'm trying to refresh the shop's image by changing the sign.
Make a fresh start with a renewed mind.

examples.ko: 이번 여행이 기분을 일신하는 계기가 되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope this trip becomes a chance to refresh my mood.
Now that the classroom has been spruced up, the students like it too.

examples.ko: 낡은 제도를 일신해야 한다는 의견이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people say the outdated system must be overhauled.

explain: '바꾸다'보다 격식 있는 말로, 분위기, 이미지, 제도, 마음가짐을 완전히 새롭게 한다는 느낌이에요. '분위기가 일신하다'처럼 자동사로도, '이미지를 일신하다'처럼 타동사로도 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '확 바꾸다'라고 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 새로 칠하고 가구를 바꿔 가게 분위기를 일신했어요.
phrases.en: We repainted and changed the furniture to refresh the shop's mood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분위기를 완전히 새롭게 바꿀 때 쓰는 대표 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The typical phrase for completely renewing an atmosphere.

phrases.en: I want to renew my mindset in the new year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음을 새롭게 다잡는다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to renew one's resolve and attitude.

phrases.en: I completely changed my hairstyle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '일신하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday alternative to 일신하다.

explain_en: It is a more formal word than '바꾸다', with the feel of making an atmosphere, image, system or mindset completely new. It works both intransitively ('분위기가 일신하다') and transitively ('이미지를 일신하다'). In daily conversation people may say '확 바꾸다'.
